newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN SHARES WEAKER,WALL ST UNDERMINES CONFIDENCE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN SHARES WEAKER,WALL ST UNDERMINES CONFIDENCE.

text.p: German shares looked set for a day of moderate losses as Tuesday's 1.26 percent slide on Wall Street, which took the Dow Jones index below the 8,000 point mark for the first time since July 21, undermined confidence.
Dealers said volumes were thin and that the market was essentially on hold, waiting for U.S. July retail sales and producer prices data due for release at 1230 GMT.

SuedwestLB futures traders said in a commentary that that DAX index, now at about 4,320 could be pulled under 4,300 by the figures. "If the 4,300 line holds at the close then today should be seen as a buy opportunity," SuedwestLB said.

Dealers said comments from the Bundesbank published this morning which showed the central bank was observing inflation trends closely and would act when necessary had been noted by the market but were having no real influence.
Financial markets are now broadly of the view that it is only a matter of time before the Bundesbank starts to tighten the monetary policy screws.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was trading down 77 points at 4,299.83 at 0840 GMT.
